text: Last Black Friday, this deal cost seventy-eight dollars more than it did a month earlier.
A smartwatch. Six hundred and two dollars in October... then six seventy-nine on Black Friday, with a sale badge on it.
A watchdog group checked three hundred fifty Amazon deals. Almost one in three were no cheaper than the month before. Nearly one in ten cost more.
One pair of boots went from ninety-eight dollars... to a hundred and eighty, as a Cyber Monday deal.
Amazon says that study is flawed, and that its own check found almost every deal was a real low.
In Europe, stores have to show the lowest price from the last thirty days. In the US, they don't.
So before you buy, paste the link into a free price tracker like Keepa or CamelCamelCamel, and look at the last thirty days.
If the line didn't drop... the deal is just a sticker.
Save this, and check before you tap buy.
